summary: Kenya abolished visas in January 2024 but replaced them with a mandatory Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) that most non-African visitors must obtain at etakenya.go.ke before departure (from USD 30); citizens of most African countries, including South Africa, are exempt from the eTA entirely, as are those of most Caribbean and Pacific island states and a few others such as Singapore, Malaysia and Cyprus.

fee.notes: From USD 30 for normal processing (up to 72 hours); expedited, immediate processing costs USD 100 more. The standard eTA allows one entry; the portal also lists a one-year multiple-entry eTA (USD 300), a five-year multiple-entry eTA for US citizens (USD 185) and a transit eTA (USD 20). It does not state how long an eTA stays valid or the length of stay it allows. Every traveller needs one, including infants and children.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Kenya itself has yellow fever risk areas, so vaccination is recommended for most visitors aged 9 months or over (generally not for trips limited to Nairobi, Mombasa and the former North Eastern and Coast provinces).

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present in most of Kenya below 2,500 m, including the coast and the main safari parks (Nairobi city is lower-risk). Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Kenya

notes: The Government of Canada says the use, manufacture or importation of plastic bags, including garbage and shopping bags, is illegal in Kenya; offenders, including tourists, can face fines of up to USD 40,000, up to two years in prison, or both.

The Kenya Revenue Authority's duty-free allowance: spirits (including liqueurs) or wine up to 1 liter, or wine up to 2 liters; perfume and toilet water up to half a liter, of which no more than a quarter may be perfume; and cigarettes, cigars, cheroots, cigarillos, tobacco and snuff up to 250 g in all.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and popular tourist destinations but not in remote locations, and that ATMs are widely available in cities. M-PESA mobile money is a common form of payment accepted across Kenya, including at national parks, which do not accept cash: they generally take credit cards, but at times only M-PESA works.

safety.text: Violent crime, including mugging, armed robbery and carjacking, is frequent in the large cities and on major highways; avoid walking alone in isolated areas, even in daylight, and take extra care in parts of Nairobi (Eastleigh, the central business district, Mathare and Kibera) and in Mombasa's Old Town and around the Likoni Ferry. The UK government advises against all travel to areas near the Somali border, including Mandera County and most of Garissa and Lamu counties, because of the risk of terrorism.

tips.text: Apply for the Kenya eTA only at the official portal etakenya.go.ke, where the fee starts at USD 30.
The Government of Canada warns that plastic bags are illegal in Kenya — using or importing them can bring fines of up to USD 40,000, up to two years in prison, or both. Use cloth or paper bags.

According to the Government of Canada, national parks do not accept cash: they generally take credit cards, but at times, because of technical problems, only M-PESA mobile money works. Check whether park fees are included in your safari price.
The Government of Canada describes M-PESA mobile money as a common form of payment accepted across Kenya, including at national parks.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya no longer issues tourist visas, but US citizens — like most non-African visitors — must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) at etakenya.go.ke before departure. It costs from USD 30 and is usually approved within 3 business days; the standard eTA allows one entry, and the portal does not state the length of stay.

faq.question: Is the Kenya eTA the same as a visa?
faq.answer: Functionally it replaced the old 50 USD eVisa in January 2024: it is a pre-travel authorization that every non-exempt visitor needs, costs from USD 30, and is applied for online at etakenya.go.ke. Citizens of most African countries and East African Community members are exempt, as are those of most Caribbean and Pacific island states, Singapore, Malaysia, Cyprus and a few others.

faq.question: How early should I apply for the Kenya eTA?
faq.answer: The official processing standard is up to 3 business days, and Kenya recommends applying at least two weeks before travel. Applications from some nationalities undergo extra vetting and can take longer, so do not leave it to the last minute — airlines check the eTA at check-in.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Kenya?
faq.answer: It is mandatory only if you are aged 1 year or over and arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. However, Kenya itself has yellow fever risk areas, so vaccination is recommended for most visitors. The Government of Canada adds that Kenyan authorities regularly carry out spot checks for proof of yellow fever vaccination, so carry a copy with you.

faq.question: When is the best time for a Kenya safari?
faq.answer: No official source gives a best safari season. The Government of Canada says Kenya's two rainy seasons usually run from October to November and from March to mid-June, varying from year to year, and that seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel. Budget for park fees, which are often charged on top of a safari price; parks do not accept cash.
